pillar_reactions.evidence: Volunteered agreement and mapped it onto his own vocabulary: 'Any of the primal movements, man, I'm down. Like, pull-ups, push-ups, squats, lunges, all that. Like, I get it. Twists. Like, I understand, like, primal movement pattern.' He had already been drawn in by the nervous-system release content specifically — 'twists and shakes and arm rattles' — which connects to the somatic coaching certification he is pursuing, making this the pillar with the deepest personal hook.

'I'm aligned with all that.' Then on fermented foods, which were new to him: 'I'm excited about that because I'm unfamiliar. I'm new to all that... and I'm wide open.' The rep screen-shared his own lunch — sweet potato fries, ground beef, beetroot kimchi, jalapeño kimchi — and it landed. A former vegan with a history of dietary discipline had no resistance to any of it.

Asked the sharpest measurement question in the batch: 'in terms of tracking, aside from photos, how is that measured? So it's like my body fat percentage, my weight initially. How am I recording that, measuring that, sharing that, and then continuing to measure and share that?' The answer — that body fat is not really tracked and the focus is compliance, session times and reps — did not appear to satisfy him. He then probed the fasting-window scheduling and closed with 'I guess I'd have to think about that', the only hesitation he expressed all call.

anchors.raw: it's not a grand a month. It's 200 bucks a month. There's no commitment in terms of time frame. So it's not like you have to sign up for six months. It's monthly rolling.
anchors.competitor: Primal University (Primal Instinct's own self-guided product)
anchors.note: Third appearance of Primal University in this batch as the answer to a high-ticket affordability objection, and the second time it replaced the sale entirely. The rep framed the comparison in explicit price terms — a grand a month versus two hundred — which is the arithmetic that beat the coaching offer on the Ad Morris call four days earlier.

anchors.raw: It will say 7800 in the top, but if you pay it off early, it reduces that load. That's just if you do the monthlies... So then to be clear, if I get accepted and it's $650 every month? It's $650 every month.
anchors.note: The financing route prices the same programme at $7,800 and the monthly route at $7,200, both above the $6,000 headline. Presenting a prospect with no cash a number 30% higher than the one he had already declined makes the offer harder, not easier — and the application was declined anyway.

anchors.raw: I pull up my old, you know, old calisthenics stuff that I used to run and I remember it and it's cool, but I'm just like, uh, I'm over it
anchors.note: A free alternative he owns, remembers and has previously succeeded with — it took him to 10-12% body fat five years ago. His objection to it is boredom rather than efficacy, which means the offer must be sold on novelty and progression. Nobody made that argument; the boredom he named as his root cause was never converted into a reason to buy.

anchors.raw: currently unemployed, coming out of pocket, don't have any credit to put it on, don't have anybody to borrow from, kind of thing
anchors.note: Not an anchor in the usual sense — an absolute constraint, stated plainly at the moment price was introduced and confirmed minutes later by a declined credit application. Recorded because the rep continued to sell against it for another five minutes rather than treating it as a disqualification.

unmet_demand.want: Objective progress measurement — body fat percentage and weight tracked and shared over time, which he asked about directly and unprompted
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep's answer was that body fat is not really tracked: 'We don't necessarily track it. It's good, like if you go get DEXAs once a month, great.' What is tracked is compliance, session duration and reps. For a prospect whose entire goal is stated numerically — 185 lb at single-digit body fat — the metric that defines success sits outside the tracking system.

unmet_demand.want: Novelty and challenge to break a plateau, which he named as his actual root cause — 'I'm bored and I don't want to do it by myself'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme almost certainly answers this — the rep described monthly plan changes, but only later, inside the Primal University pitch, and never connected it to the boredom the prospect had already identified. The single strongest available buying argument was left on the floor.

unmet_demand.want: Advice on which kettlebell to buy before starting, given he owns none
unmet_demand.why_unmet: In the coaching offer this is answered on the onboarding call. In the product he was actually sold, it is not: 'Is there a spot in here where it advises me on the kettlebells? Cause I don't have kettlebells yet.' / 'No, but you can ask on the live call.' A prospect with no equipment and no income is being routed to a self-guided library that cannot tell him what to buy.
